children: Alphabet, Google's search and cloud parent

, has an AI challenge: turning more queries into more advertising dollars. Shares rose 1.85% to $285.01 at 9:40 a.m. ET on November 2, even as Wells Fargo lowered its price target to $365 from $371 while keeping an Overweight rating. Search remains the bigger revenue engine, generating more than twice Google Cloud's quarterly sales.

Wells Fargo pins much of the search slowdown on AI Overviews and expects that pressure to last another two quarters. That remains the firm's assessment. Alphabet's October 28 results put Search and other revenue at $63.350 billion, compared with Cloud's $30.709 billion. Cloud delivered $11.121 billion in operating income, implying a 36.2% operating margin. Strong profitability gives Cloud weight, but its revenue still amounts to just 48.5% of Search's total.

The GuruFocus snapshot shows a GF Score of 98/100, with profitability and growth leading the scorecard, alongside three medium warning signs. That points to business strength while leaving the search monetization question open. Investors have two numbers to watch: Cloud's operating margin and Search's revenue growth. Holding the first while improving the second could offer stronger evidence that Alphabet's AI push is translating into financial gains.

title: Alphabet Stocks Rise 1.85% With Search Monetization Behind Wells Fargo's Target Cut
